topSignals.title: Bloom Energy +10% on July 29 as post-Q2 analyst consensus lifts to $280
topSignals.text: — Following yesterday's record Q2 blowout (revenue $1.065B, EPS $0.78 — beating by 29% and 90%), BE traded +10% on July 29, implying ~$203 from the $184.89 pre-earnings close. Average analyst price target lifted to $280.46 (27 analysts: 8 Strong Buy, 2 Moderate Buy, 16 Hold, 1 Strong Sell). CEO KR Sridhar on the Q2 call: "Order backlog is outpacing revenue." Full post-earnings upgrade cycle expected in the next 48-72 hrs. Key pending: Q2 transcript (expected July 30-31) for shipped MW, scandium supply chain statement, and Fremont utilization disclosure. TipRanks | StockTwits | TheStreet

topSignals.title: NM AG opens criminal investigation into fraudulent Project Jupiter public comments
topSignals.text: — New Mexico AG Raúl Torrez formally opened an investigation into allegations that public comment letters supporting Project Jupiter's air quality permit application were submitted "fraudulently" under residents' and local officials' names without their knowledge — including via official .gov email addresses. The same day (July 28), a community meeting in Santa Teresa reportedly turned "chaotic." Oracle denied canvasser involvement and said it would not condone abuse of its public comment portal. This is a new legal/criminal dimension stacked on top of the existing air permit hearing (October 19) and gas pipeline blockers. Source NM | ABQ Journal | KRWG

topSignals.title: Oracle counters with $4.7B economic impact data as Project Jupiter PR battle escalates
topSignals.text: — Oracle published a July 28 press release quantifying Project Jupiter's economic footprint: ~$80M in state/local tax revenue generated Jan-May 2026, $4.7B projected long-term impact, 7,000 construction jobs, 1,500 ongoing positions. The PR offensive launched the same day the AG investigation became public and the community meeting turned contentious — signaling an escalating battle over the project's permit fate ahead of the October 19 hearing. Oracle PR July 28 | KFOX TV

items.text: Elcogen: No new announcements July 29. EFCF 2026 proceedings embargo now on day 26+ (exceeds typical 2-3 week post-conference window); papers likely in journal peer-review queue. E3000 G2 deliveries ongoing; ELCO I factory (360 MW/yr, Tallinn) in volume production. Watch elcogen.com for embargo lift.

Topsoe: No new SOFC/SOEC announcements July 29. Herning SOEC factory (440 jobs, 500 MW/yr capacity) remains hibernated pending demand inflection. Active focus: green ammonia ($1.6B Jordan FEED) and eSAF licensing. SOFC data-center pathway deferred to 2029+ per H2 access constraints.

MS-SOFC 2026 reviews (Springer): Two comprehensive reviews confirmed published in 2026. (1) "Comprehensive review of current trends and future directions of metal-supported solid oxide fuel cell: From materials to applications," Int. J. Minerals, Metallurgy and Materials — doi:10.1007/s12613-026-3402-0. (2) "A comprehensive review on the progress and evaluation of metal supported solid oxide fuel cells," J. Solid State Electrochemistry — doi:10.1007/s10008-026-06571-7. Both confirm MS-SOFC advantages over ceramic SOFCs: rapid start-up, enhanced thermal cycle tolerance, lower manufacturing cost — the emerging alternative cell architecture worth tracking for next-generation capex inputs.

Oracle Project Jupiter (2.45 GW): See Top Signals #2 and #3. AG criminal investigation + chaotic July 28 community meeting add new jeopardy. Oracle's $4.7B economic PR is a counter-offensive. Air permit hearing October 19 unchanged. Gas pipeline dead-end unchanged. SemiAnalysis 2029 first-power base case remains operative.

Background (unchanged): 32% of US data centers planning fully off-grid SOFC by 2030 per survey of 152 industry insiders. Crusoe/Tallgrass Cheyenne 900 MW Phase 1 (Bloom, H2 2026 target), FCEL/Fit Energy 380 MW, Equinix 100+ MW, AEP/Bloom Wyoming 1 GW (2030) — no new updates July 29.

FERC RM26-4 — 19 days to August 17; ISO-NE abeyance due August 3 (5 days): No new filings reported July 29. Key pending: ISO-NE's abeyance request (August 3) — if granted, it defers tariff reform filings to a November 16 stakeholder deadline instead of the August 17 hard deadline. Outcome shapes whether avoided transmission cost ($5-20/MWh) can be modeled as LCOE input in PJM, MISO, CAISO, and ISO-NE scenarios. FERC RM26-4 | Day Pitney / ISO-NE memo

NM Project Jupiter AG investigation: See Top Signal #2. Criminal investigation dimension now on record. Raises probability that air permit faces procedural complications or delay beyond the October 19 hearing.

Microsoft TMI Unit 1 (835 MW nuclear, PA): FERC transmission waiver cleared "the last major grid obstacle" in mid-2026. Commercial operation targeted second half of 2027. Structural note: even the fastest nuclear restart remains 12-18 months away from first electrons, vs. SOFC's 90-day deployment — SOFC retains near-term advantage for AI data centers requiring power before 2027. Introl Blog
Meta nuclear portfolio: Up to 6.6 GW across TerraPower (Natrium SFR), Oklo (Aurora SFR), Vistra, and Constellation. All 2030+ timelines. SMR Intel
No new announcements July 29. Background CCGT/battery LCOE benchmarks unchanged.

Bloom Energy (BE): +10% session July 29 (~$203 implied from $184.89 pre-earnings close). Analyst consensus: avg. PT $280.46 (27 analysts: 8 Strong Buy, 2 Moderate Buy, 16 Hold, 1 Strong Sell). JPMorgan PT $346, Overweight (July 21 upgrade). Full post-earnings upgrade cycle underway — expect 3-5 formal target raises in next 48-72 hours. TipRanks | Yahoo Finance analyst upgrades | Quiver Quantitative
FuelCell Energy (FCEL): ~$21.37, no new announcements July 29. $200M equity offering (July 7) and Siemens EBOP MOU (July 9) are the most recent substantive events.
Ceres Power (LON: CWR): ~-40% MTD on London Stock Exchange. No new catalyst or exchange announcement. H1 2026 results (September) remain next scheduled event.
MS-SOFC 2026 reviews: See Stack & Cell above. Both confirm manufacturing cost as the key commercial differentiator for MS-SOFC vs. ceramic SOFCs; neither provides new performance benchmark data.
Bloom Q2 transcript pending: Expected July 30-31. Extract targets: shipped MW in Q2 (for cost/kW derivation), scandium supply chain statement, Fremont utilization/expansion, EaaS $/MWh disclosure.

RSC Green Chemistry, Vol. 26 (2026): "Techno-economic analysis of solid oxide fuel cell-based energy systems for decarbonising residential power and heat in the United Kingdom." CHP system analysis; H2-fed SOFC achieves 92.12% system efficiency vs. 66.98% for NG-fed. RSC — LCOE flag: H2 fuel-switching premium quantifiable from this study; UK cost curves bracket distributed SOFC deployment economics at residential/small-commercial scale.

ScienceDirect, Fuel/Elsevier (2025): "Comparative techno-economic assessment of solid oxide fuel cells versus hydrogen-fueled internal combustion engines for institutional energy management." Direct capex/opex comparison at institutional load scales (comparable to small data center). ScienceDirect — LCOE flag: Provides SOFC vs. competing DG technology cost inputs at building-scale; confirms SOFC economic competitiveness even before ITC 48E and avoided grid cost credits.

lcoe.text: BE Q2 product margin 33.4% → capex trajectory pending transcript: Product revenue $935.4M at Fremont 2 GW/yr capacity implies rough $468/kW realized product price (estimated; excludes EaaS/service mix and exact shipped MW). Margin improvement of +668bp YoY strongly signals declining stack manufacturing cost. Do NOT update base capex until shipped MW confirmed from Q2 transcript (July 30-31).

Post-earnings upgrade cycle → discount rate proxy: Analyst avg. PT $280.46 (27 analysts). Formal upgrades in next 48-72 hrs will update the market cost-of-capital proxy for the LCOE model discount rate sensitivity.

RSC Green Chemistry 2026 UK CHP TEA: H2-fed SOFC system efficiency 92.12% vs. NG-fed 66.98% — the 25pp premium quantifies the H2 fuel-switch LCOE improvement as an input for fuel-switching sensitivity analysis in the model.

Jupiter risk premium escalation: NM AG criminal investigation + chaotic public meeting raises probability of "Jupiter delayed to 2029" scenario. Recommend raising scenario weight from ~25% to ~40% in the pipeline model (additive to the 0.5-1.0 GW reduction flagged July 28). Combined: modeled 2026-2027 installed GW should be reduced by 0.7-1.3 GW in the bear scenario.
